$comment: Canary specs for the worker pipeline (#1878). Config-as-data, same convention as
Each canary is a FIXED issue whose correct outcome is known in advance, re-dispatched on
demand. `expect` keys must exist in ASSERTIONS (scripts/canary.mjs) — an unknown key FAILS
rather than passing silently, so the rig cannot quietly stop checking.
`issue: null` means the canary is specified but not yet wired to a real ticket; the verify
workflow skips it and says so. Fill in the number once the ticket exists.
Two failure classes are covered on purpose (#1876 + #1885): the pipeline BREAKING, and the
pipeline running perfectly while shipping something incomplete.

canaries.why: #1876 defect 1 — the last file of a commit bucket was dropped, and the dropped one was the only file that mattered. Also #1874's shape: a locale-only change must NOT be held by the tests gate.
canaries.task: change a string in three of a package's locale files

canaries.why: The acceptance gate's happy path — an apps/ change must resolve an APP_DIR and typecheck clean.
canaries.task: a one-line, behaviour-free change in an app the acceptance gate can typecheck

canaries.why: A genuinely broken deliverable must open as a DRAFT so automerge (#339) skips it. If this canary ever goes non-draft, red work can land.
canaries.task: a change that fails the touched app's typecheck

canaries.why: #1885 — the worker shipped #1875's logic with none of its five agreed tests, and every check went green. Clause (7) now requires the test; this asserts it actually appears.
canaries.task: a small hand-written logic change under packages/, with the issue naming its test cases

canaries.why: The one canary that SHOULD produce nothing. It guards the artifact-gate's honesty: no PR is correct here, but the failure comment must not assert a cause it never checked (#1751, #1876 defect 3).
canaries.task: an issue whose work is already done, so there is nothing to build
